reason: A disc or calyx that is rim-like is a low ring round the receptacle or a gland. PATO ring shaped (EXACT synonym annular) covers it. A calyx 'reduced to a rim' can also take the vestigial rule.
Tasteless or insipid fruit, wood or mesocarp means lacking flavour: PATO:0001330 flavourless. 'Without the taste of wintergreen' denies one particular taste and is only loosely covered.
Well-spaced flowers, lobes or veins are widely separated from the nearest structures of their kind, which is the definition of FLOPO distant.
Narrow-elliptic is elliptic with a high length-to-width ratio. 'Narrow' is a degree word, so the shape is PATO elliptic, and any stated ratio goes to pattern 11.

label: polyhedral
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being bounded by several more or less flat faces that meet at distinct angles, as in seeds pressed against one another in a fruit.
reason: There is no PATO term for a many-faced solid. PATO:0001977 angular is about salient angles on a margin, not about flat faces.

label: lemon-scented
definition: An odorous quality inhering in a plant structure by virtue of its having an odour like that of lemon peel.
reason: A frequent, well-defined scent. It is a sibling of FLOPO sweet-scented, spicy-scented and sour-smelling, which have the same parent.
The surface is canescent and 'appressed' describes the hairs, not the surface. The firm content is FLOPO canescent. The hair position can be added as appressed (FLOPO:0991064) on the trichomes.
A hyphenated compound of two shapes, ovoid (PATO:0001891) and subglobose, meaning intermediate between them. This is the continuum pattern, not a term.
A ratio of two dimensions of the same part (width:height > 1) with no number. FLOPO depressed is close for fruits but does not fit discs, stigmas or sepals.

target: new: quality of a part of the bearer (vein colour)
reason: The colour belongs to the veins (PO:0005020 vascular bundle) of the petal or sepal, not to the bearer itself: has part some (vein and has characteristic some dark colour). Several statements also carry a degree (±) or frequency (often).

'Inflorescence a thyrse' gives the inflorescence's architecture. PO uses 'thyrse' as a synonym of both PO:0030127 indeterminate and PO:0030128 determinate thyrse inflorescence, so it cannot pick one bearer. FLOPO thyrse-like holds for either.
Varnished leaves and fruits have a high-gloss surface, as if lacquered: PATO glistening (EXACT synonyms glossy, shiny). This follows the earlier rule for 'lustrous'.
A count of seeds (PO:0009010) in the fruit, given with the vague number 'several'. This is the count-of-parts pattern.

target: comparison or relation stated without its second term
reason: A superlative without the set it ranks in, or the position of the widest point along the organ. Same as the earlier decision for 'broadest'.
In these floras 'ungulate' is a misspelling of unguiculate (see 'base long ungulate' and the French 'onguiculés'), meaning clawed. 'Hoof-shaped' does not fit petals, sepals or bracts.
It does not say what the pattern is (colour, sculpture or flaking). Several statements also only compare with another part ('patterned similar to the petiole').
A compound of two margin values, crenulate (PATO:0001889 scalloped) and serrulate (FLOPO:0991081), meaning teeth intermediate between them. This is the continuum pattern.
A bladdery calyx or fruit is thin-walled and blown up like a bladder, filled with air: PATO inflated. 'Not bladdery' is its negation.
Stems, achenes and fruits with blunt angles are angular. 'Obtusely' is the degree of the angle, which PATO does not split.
Two qualities of different parts run together: the outline is ovate (FLOPO:0991024, 'broadly' as degree) and the apex is acuminate (PATO:0002228). It needs two annotations, not one term.
Nutlets or achenes enveloped by the perigynium or perianth: PATO:0005016 surrounded by, towards the enveloping part. Without that second term the statement should be rejected, as for 'covered'.

label: julaceous
definition: A cylindrical quality inhering in a leafy shoot by virtue of its leaves being closely imbricate and appressed, so that the shoot is smooth, round in section and catkin-like.
reason: A standard bryological shoot shape (159 statements). It is not the same as terete or imbricate alone, because it combines a round section with tightly overlapping leaves.

A length measurement whose bearer is the claw of the petal (part of the petal). The bearer needs a petal claw class, since 'claw' alone was rejected as a generic part. The quality is length with a range.

label: scapiform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being a long, leafless or nearly leafless axis arising at or near the base of the plant and bearing flowers at its tip, like a scape.
reason: A frequent quality of peduncles and stems with no term. It is a sibling of FLOPO spike-like and raceme-like, like PATO corymb-like.

label: parted
definition: A split quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being divided more than halfway, but not fully, to its base or midrib into segments.
reason: A standard degree in botany's lobed–cleft–parted–divided series, deeper than lobed. It would be the parent of FLOPO:0991156 pinnatipartite. Numbered forms ('3-parted') go to the count pattern.
The negation of FLOPO clawed.

label: mammillose
definition: A texture quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's surface cells each bulging outward as a whole into a low, nipple-like protuberance into which the cell lumen extends.
reason: Bryologists keep this apart from FLOPO:0991059 papillose, whose papillae are small outgrowths of the cell wall. The two are often contrasted in the same sentence ('mammillose or papillose').
Fistulose scapes, stems and leaves are hollow and tube-like: PATO hollow.
Puberulent with gland-tipped hairs. FLOPO glandular-pubescent (at least some hairs gland-tipped) covers it. The very short hair length is a degree, which puberulous (FLOPO:0991049) states on its own.
Moss leaf cells that are rectangular and several times longer than wide. 'Long' is the length-to-width degree (pattern 11 when a ratio is given), so the shape is PATO rectangular.
